newsitem.title: USA: Lands' End combats effect of UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: Lands' End combats effect of UPS strike.

text.p: Lands' End Inc, seeking to combat a slowdown since the United Parcel Service strike began, said Friday it would ship replacement goods to customers who do not receive merchandise within a week.
Lands' End said it has been shipping goods via priority mail through the U.S. Postal Service and customers have been receiving packages in four to five days.
Still customers appear to be worried about receiving goods on time because Lands' End has experienced a slowdown in calls since the UPS strike began.

To relieve those concerns, the company said it would immediately ship a replacement to any customer who does not receive an order in a week of shipment. The company also said it would advertise the guarantee in national newspapers and on CBS radio.
On Thursday, Lands' End said it has received fewer customer calls since the UPS strike began.
